title: Supply Chain Manager, Data Operations
description:
Who We Are

Verkada is transforming how organizations protect their people and places with an integrated, privacy-sensitive AI-powered platform that includes solutions for video security, access control, air quality sensors, alarms, intercoms, and visitor management. 

We’ve got serious momentum in the market: more than 30,000 customers (including 100+ of the Fortune 500), a $5.8B valuation , more than $1 billion in annualized bookings, and backing from CapitalG, Sequoia Capital, General Catalyst, Felicis Ventures, Next47 and more. Physical AI is one of the most consequential technology shifts of our time, and Verkada is at the center of it.

You can look at all kinds of communities to see our platform’s impact in the world. It's the retailer that uses our agentic AI to deter theft before it happens. The warehouse that uses AI-powered alerts to make sure its team is protected on the floor with proper PPE. The school that’s alerted to a threat in real-time and triggers a lockdown in seconds, not minutes. We’re rapidly scaling this impact: today, more than 2 million Verkada devices are deployed across 170+ countries. 

About the Role

Our team drives global demand and supply planning across all hardware product lines, optimizing forward and reverse inventory across regional warehouses to fulfill customer demand.

As our planning systems and processes continue to evolve with the growing business and the data layer that connects them, we're looking for a data steward to own the foundational data engine and operational processes powering our end-to-end planning ecosystem. You'll build, monitor, and maintain the connected data flows that our planners, cross-functional stakeholders, and external suppliers all depend on to drive daily execution.

We are committed to a thriving in-office culture. This role requires that you be on-site at our office in San Mateo, CA 5 days a week.

What You'll Do

• Foundational Data & Pipeline Ownership: Own and govern the core data layer and automated pipelines powering our planning processes - including item master data, lead times, and purchase orders - as it flows between systems. Build and maintain reliable, reusable datasets to ensure high-integrity data flows and reliable system syncs across product lines, regional warehouses, and external suppliers.

• System Health & Incident Triage: Serve as the first line of defense for planning pipeline failures and system discrepancies. Rapidly trace data sync errors, diagnose root causes across connected platforms, and drive fixes with internal/external partners.

• Data Operations & Refresh Execution: Own and run the operational cadence that keeps planning data trustworthy over time. Drive recurring data load and refresh schedules to completion, enforce automated quality checks, manage change control for data updates, and convert manual, repetitive data workflows into scalable, automated processes.

• Reporting & Analytics: Partner with team members to build operational dashboards that power day-to-day execution. Collaborate with supply chain leadership to define impact metrics and transform raw data into actionable insights.

What You Bring

• Experience: 4+ years in Data Operations, Supply Chain Analytics, Analytics Engineering, or Business Intelligence. Direct supply chain/manufacturing data experience preferred.

• Systems & Domain Knowledge: Experience with ERPs (NetSuite), supply chain planning platforms, and warehouse management systems.

• Technical Toolkit: Advanced SQL (BigQuery, Snowflake), experience with cloud data warehouses, and comfort building automation in Google Apps Script, Python, or similar scripting tools. Familiarity with Excel/Google Sheets modeling required.

• Data Operations & Process Discipline: Experience managing data refresh SLAs, monitoring pipeline execution, and building operational workflows to ensure system health and data accuracy under tight deadlines.

Watershed https://watershed.com/ is the enterprise sustainability platform. Companies like Airbnb, Carlyle Group, FedEx, Visa, and Dr. Martens use Watershed to manage climate and ESG data, produce audit-ready metrics for voluntary and regulatory reporting including CSRD, and drive real decarbonization. We are looking for team members who love product-building, want to work hard at a mission-oriented startup, and will collaborate with us in shaping the culture of a growing team.

We have offices in San Francisco, New York, Denver, London, Paris, Berlin, Sydney, Mexico City, and remote team members across the US and Europe. We hope that you'll be interested in joining us!

THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Corporate FP&A Manager to own our corporate financial model and serve as a primary finance partner to our Product, Customer, Business Foundation and Executive team.

Reporting to our Head of Finance, you will lead managing budget and forecast processes, variance analysis, and shaping how we measure and communicate company performance. You will work closely with our Founders, executive leadership, and key cross-functional partners to ensure financial rigor and visibility across the organization.

What You Will Do

Corporate Planning & Consolidation

- Lead Company-Wide Planning & Forecasting: own the short and long-term corporate financial models as well as planning processes to ensure accuracy and agility in planning across revenue, headcount, expenses, and cash flow including tax forecasting and infrastructure planning

- Lead monthly and quarterly close, board and investor reporting: budget vs. actual analysis at both corporate and departmental levels. Owning core SaaS metrics: Gross Margin %, Magic Number, Cash Burn Multiple, Rule of 40

- Drive the cash model: to guide capital allocation

- Translate complex financial data: into clear insights that drive operational performance and executive decision-making

Expense & Business Partnership

- Finance partner to Product, Engineering, Design & Science on spend and resourcing decisions

- Partner with Business Foundation and the Customer org to align resourcing with demand, watching gross margin

- Own headcount and opex planning with department heads

What You Will Bring

- 6-8+ years in FP&A, Strategic Finance, or Investment Banking / Venture Capital / Private Equity, including 2+ years inside a high-growth B2B SaaS company

- Strong financial modeling, P&L management, forecasting, and annual / long-range planning experience

- Deep understanding of SaaS metrics and recurring revenue mechanics

- Proven business partnering: able to translate complex financials for non-finance leaders and push back when it matters

- Nice to have: experience with NetSuite, Salesforce, and/or Rippling (or equivalent CRM/ERP/HRIS platforms)

Must be willing to work from an office 4 days per week (except for remote roles)

Watershed has hub offices in San Francisco, New York, London, and Mexico City and satellite offices in Denver, Sydney, Paris, and Berlin. Where we have offices, employees are expected to be in office for 4 days per week. Certain jobs are open to being remote and will be specifically noted on the jobs page and in the job description if so.

What’s the interview process like?

It starts the same for every candidate: getting to know the team members through 1 to 2 conversations about Watershed, your experience, and your interests. Next steps can vary by role, but usual next steps are a skill or experience interview (e.g. a coding interview for an engineer, a portfolio review for a designer, deeper experience call for other roles) which leads to a virtual or in person interview panel. We prioritize transparency and lack of surprise throughout the process.

title: Global Management Trainee Program
description:
About Flowmingo AI
Flowmingo is a Y Combinator-backed startup (plus VinaCapital & top global investors) on a mission to democratize hiring. We believe the current hiring model is broken: recruiters only have time to interview 5% of applicants, leaving 95% of talent-the "hidden gems"-undiscovered. We are fixing this with an AI-native, high-volume interviewing platform. Our model is unique: we offer our tool for free to recruiters to capture the massive, uncontested markets of Southeast Asia, LATAM, and Africa. This allows us to process massive volumes of candidates that traditional, expensive platforms cannot touch.
Global Management Trainee Program
(2-Year Remote Track | Intern & Early Career)
The Role
We are looking for structured, high-agency operators to join our 2-year Global Management Trainee Program. This is a fast-track leadership development initiative designed to build the next generation of operators and managers at Flowmingo.
This is a hands-on, cross-functional role: you will rotate across core business areas, learn how an AI startup operates at scale, and eventually own a function or region. You’ll be accountable for delivering results in a high-growth, remote-first environment.
Program Tracks:

• Intern Track (Part-Time): Minimum 20 hours per week, 24-month structured program for final-year students or fresh graduates.

• Early Career Track (Full-Time): 24-month accelerated pathway for professionals with 0-3 years of experience.

What You’ll Own (24-Month Roadmap)

• Phase 1 (0-6 Months): Foundations of Execution. Support live projects across functions, track KPIs, and improve internal workflows.

• Phase 2 (6-12 Months): Cross-Functional Rotation. Rotate through 2-3 core functions (Growth, Operations, Product, or Monetization). Lead scoped initiatives and own small KPIs.

• Phase 3 (12-18 Months): Initiative Leadership. Lead cross-functional projects, manage junior team members, and design scalable operational systems.

• Phase 4 (18-24 Months): Management Evaluation. Own a specific function or major initiative. Evaluate readiness for transition into permanent managerial roles.

What We Look For

• High Agency: You don’t wait for instructions; you find ways to make things happen.

• Systems Thinking: You think in frameworks and understand how to design scalable systems rather than just fixing individual problems.

• Intellectual Rigor: Strong academic or professional performance with the ability to communicate clearly in written English.

• Comfort with Ambiguity: You thrive in a fast-paced startup environment where the path isn't always marked.

• Emerging Market Empathy: You are curious about technology and its impact on the Global South.

Why This Program is Different

• Direct Impact: You won't be doing "busy work." You will be shipping features and systems that thousands of candidates use.

• Elite Peers: Work alongside team members from top institutions (YC, UPenn, NYU, etc.) and learn from founders directly.

• YC Network: Gain access to one of the most powerful startup networks in the world.

• Remote-First Excellence: Learn how to operate effectively in an async-first, global company.

Application Process
We don’t believe in long, drawn-out processes, but we do screen for the top tier. If you are interested in this opportunity, please click the 'Apply Now' button to submit your application. We will inform you regarding the next steps within 1-3 working days if you are a good fit.

title: Full Stack Engineer - Cloud & SaaS Integrations
description:
Location
Our Full Stack Software Engineer will be an integral part of our R&D team. This role is based remotely as a full-time employee in the UK, Ireland, Estonia, the Netherlands, Sweden and Israel. We are also open to contractors in Eastern Europe and Portugal.
Who We Are
DoiT is a global technology company that works with cloud-driven organizations to leverage the cloud to drive business growth and innovation. We combine data, technology, and human expertise to ensure our customers operate in a well-architected and scalable state - from planning to production.
Delivering DoiT Cloud Intelligence, the only solution that integrates advanced technology with human intelligence, we help our customers solve complex multicloud problems and drive efficiency.With decades of multicloud experience, we have specializations in Kubernetes, GenAI, CloudOps, and more. An award-winning strategic partner of AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure, we work alongside more than 4,000 customers worldwide.
The Opportunity
Cloud spend is no longer just AWS, Google Cloud and Azure. Our customers now run a large and growing share of their technology spend through SaaS platforms, data clouds and AI vendors - and every one of those vendors is an integration that brings another slice of their spend into view.
You'll own DoiT's Integrations Framework and the experience built on top of it. This is a chance to define what a great integration experience looks like: a customer connects a new vendor in minutes, sees at a glance that their data is flowing, and handles credential rotation, reconnects and backfills themselves without thinking twice. On the framework side, you'll make adding the next vendor a small, well-understood piece of work rather than a project - so coverage grows as fast as the vendor landscape does.
You'll work AI-augmented from day one. Integration development is spec-driven work against constantly changing third-party APIs: one of the highest-leverage places to apply agentic AI tooling. We expect you to use it across your whole workflow and to have real opinions about where it earns its place.
Responsibilities

•
Building new integrations. This is the core of the role. Design and ship integrations against third-party billing and usage APIs - authentication, incremental sync, rate limits, error handling, schema drift - and invest in the Integrations Framework itself, along with testing harnesses and scaffolding, so the tenth integration takes a fraction of the effort of the first.

•
Working AI-augmented. Use AI daily across the full span of your work - exploring unfamiliar codebases and third-party APIs, prototyping approaches, generating and reviewing code, debugging, writing tests, and producing documentation. Push on what agentic tooling can do for this codebase, and bring judgement about where AI raises velocity and where a human still has to hold the quality bar.

•
Integration management experience. Build the interfaces customers use to connect, configure and trust their integrations: health and status visibility, actionable error states, credential and key rotation, and clear feedback when something needs attention.

•
Self-service by default. Design self-service into the framework from the start - backfills, reconnects and diagnostics that customers and internal teams run themselves.

•
API-first. Build capabilities so they're fully available through APIs, not just the UI. Both humans and agents should be able to drive the platform.

•
Implementing features end-to-end. From proposal, through spec and implementation, to maintenance. You're expected to propose things you think would be a good addition, not wait for a spec.

Qualifications

• 3+ years of professional software engineering experience, shipping and owning features in production

• Strong TypeScript , including modern frontend work - React preferred

• Hands-on experience with Go , or strong backend experience in another language (Python, Java, Node.js, C#) with genuin

title: Senior WAF Migration Engineer
description:
Drive secure, seamless WAF migrations across complex enterprise environments.

The Role

As a Senior WAF Migration Engineer, you will provide hands-on technical delivery for the migration of Web Application Firewall (WAF) capabilities to Cloudflare and/or Akamai. You will work closely with architecture, security, network, and application teams to execute migration waves, onboard applications, implement security policies, and support successful cutovers.

You will play a key role in validating functionality, security, and performance, resolving technical issues, and supporting post-migration stabilization across complex enterprise environments.

What You’ll Do

• Deliver end-to-end WAF migrations to Cloudflare and/or Akamai, including configuration, application onboarding, and deployment.

• Implement and tune WAF security policies, rules, and controls in line with application and security requirements.

• Execute DNS and traffic-routing changes and support integrations required for successful application migration.

• Perform testing, troubleshooting, and validation to confirm functionality, security, and performance throughout migration waves.

• Partner with architecture, security, network, and application teams to support cutover activities, resolve technical issues, and stabilize services following migration.

What We’re Looking For

• 7+ years of relevant experience in network security, application security, infrastructure engineering, or related technical roles, with substantial hands-on WAF experience.

• Strong hands-on experience configuring, migrating, and supporting enterprise WAF technologies, ideally Cloudflare and/or Akamai.

• Practical knowledge of DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, TLS, traffic routing, application delivery, and web security concepts.

• Experience implementing and tuning WAF policies and security rules, troubleshooting application traffic, and resolving migration or production issues.

• Demonstrated experience working collaboratively with architecture, security, network, and application teams to deliver complex technical changes.

Bonus Points For

• Experience delivering large-scale WAF migration or modernization programs across complex enterprise environments.

• Knowledge of Cloudflare and Akamai security, application delivery, and traffic management capabilities.

• Experience supporting phased application migration waves, production cutovers, and post-deployment stabilization.

• Familiarity with automation, scripting, APIs, or infrastructure-as-code approaches used to support security or infrastructure deployments.

• Experience delivering security technology within financial services or another highly regulated environment.

Why Join Capco

• Deliver high-impact technology solutions for Tier 1 financial institutions

• Work in a collaborative, flat, and entrepreneurial consulting culture

• Access continuous learning, training, and industry certifications

• Be part of a team shaping the future of digital financial services

Audit & Inspection Leadership

• Lead, coordinate and support PV inspection readiness activities and contribute to regulatory health authority inspections conduct and management

•
Quality Systems & Risk Management

• Develop/improve and manage quality systems and processes:

• Enhance PV risk-based audit strategy and annual assessment processes in line with regulatory requirements, changing product profile, emerging markets and business dev.

• Responsible for managing/overseeing routine/for cause audits of vendors, partners, processes, affiliate etc.

• Supporting the activities related to the vendor management processes and assessments as well as sub-contractors, etc.

• Conducting/managing review of key PV procedures and documents

• Developing quality KPI’s and metrics and measures to drive assessment and continuous improvement

•
Vendor Oversight

• Strong global knowledge and understanding of international PV regulations applicable to the conduct of clinical trials and pharmacovigilance operations

•
Metrics & Continuous Improvement

• Keep up to date with knowledge of GVP requirements and implement them in GVP QA procedures and day to day tasks

• Develop tools and assessment improvements using AI to increase efficiency in routine processes

• Participate and support as backup to the Head, GVP QA to enhance performance and maintain accountability for the implementation of BeOne QA systems

•
Cross-functional Leadership

• Coordinate / cooperate with interfacing departments such as Global Patient Safety, Regulatory Affairs, Medical affairs, Clinical operations, Quality to ensure implementation of PV requirements.

• Superb attention to detail, excellent review skills and the ability to organize and manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment

Du administrierst MySQL in Produktion: Backups, Performance, Recovery

Du bist Sparringspartner für Engineering, Data und Product - und erklärst, warum Dinge so gebaut sind, wie sie gebaut sind

Mehrjährige Erfahrung im Betrieb von Linux-Serverumgebungen (Debian/Ubuntu) - du weißt, wie man Systeme auch ohne Assistenz von A nach B bringt
Fundierte Netzwerkkenntnisse: TCP/IP, Routing, DNS, Load Balancing, Firewall- und VPN-Administration

Ansible in Produktion, Container

Gryps is an AI operating system for the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry. Institutional owners such as hospital systems, universities, and airport authorities run multi-billion-dollar capital programs on data scattered across emails, spreadsheets, network drives, and disconnected systems of record. Gryps connects that information and gives owner teams an AI operating system for their capital programs, so they can find answers, manage risk, automate their work and make decisions faster.

We are a product-focused organization that dreams big and achieves those dreams. Our customers are large players in the construction industry. This is an opportunity to be part of a nimble team where every individual is an expert in their area. We work fast, iterate quickly, and create a product that transforms how our customers work through AI.

This is the place for you if you’ve worked in a role at the intersection of AI, automation, data analytics, construction tech, construction management, and innovative technology-and you’re looking for the next leap in your career. You will have direct influence over the growth of Gryps within customer organizations, our product roadmap, and impact on the Gryps bottom line.

We’re a growing company backed by Primary Ventures, LDV Capital, Pear VC, and other top investors. You will work directly with the CEO and our customers-large organizations that own and operate hospitals, universities, and public infrastructure.

THE ROLE

We're hiring a Head of AI Deployment to lead a team of 4-6 in turning Gryps deployments into measurable value for our customers. You'll own the full post-sale relationship: understanding each customer's program, designing the data strategy behind their deployment, identifying the use cases that matter most, guiding the implementation team to fast, repeatable time to value, and measuring the success of the deployment.

This is a player-coach role. You'll work directly with owner executives and program leaders while developing early-career professionals into strong implementers and advisors. You'll also be accountable for renewals and expansion, because customers who get real value are the ones who grow with us.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

LEAD AND DEVELOP THE TEAM

- Manage, coach, and grow a team of 4-6 customer success and implementation professionals, many early in their careers. Set clear expectations, give direct feedback, and build their construction domain knowledge and client-facing confidence.

- Build the playbooks, standards, and rituals that make delivery consistent: onboarding frameworks, implementation checklists, account reviews, and health scoring.

DEFINE VALUE AND DATA STRATEGY

- Work with customers to find the highest-value use cases across their capital programs, such as cost and change tracking, schedule risk, document and contract intelligence, closeout, and portfolio reporting. Prioritize them by business impact and feasibility.

- Design the data strategy for each use case: which sources to connect, how unstructured and structured data is organized and validated, and how outputs tie back to the customer's systems of record and decisions.

- Turn customer outcomes into clear, quantified value stories that executives and champions can carry into their own organizations.

OWN CUSTOMER RELATIONSHIPS

- Serve as trusted advisor and executive sponsor for your accounts, from project and program managers up to VPs of Facilities, Capital Planning, and Real Estate.

- Lead executive business reviews that connect product usage to program outcomes and set the agenda for what comes next.

- Represent the customer's voice internally, partnering with Product and Engineering on requirements, feedback, and roadmap priorities.

DRIVE PRODUCT ENGAGEMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION EFFICIENCY

- Own adoption and engagement metrics across your book of business. Spot drifting accounts early and step in before they become risks.

- Run implementation for speed

title: Customer Success Engineer (Internship)
description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!
Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.
Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times.
To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.
BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.
Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.
Location
This is a six-month internship based at our HQ in central Zurich or in Munich. This is an in-person role. You learn this job by sitting next to people who already do it, and that does not work remotely.
About the role
Think of this role as the modern Sherlock Holmes - new puzzles to solve and new people to work with, every single day.
This role sits exactly at the intersection of technology and business, and that is not a figure of speech. On one side you are in the system, in the data, working out what actually happened. On the other you are on a call with a finance team explaining it and agreeing what to do. You need both, every day.
Our customers run their finance and supply chain processes on blp. When something does not behave the way they expected, a document that did not post, an exception that should have resolved itself, a number in a dashboard that looks wrong, they write to us. That is where your work starts, and it is also where you become the face of blp for that customer. What reaches them is you: your answer, your explanation, your judgement about what to do next.
You will not be reading from a script and escalating. You investigate what the system did, what the data says and what the customer's process actually requires. You have the access and the authority to change configuration when that is the answer. And when it is not, you know who to bring in and what to give them.
The role grows with you. You start on cases where the pattern is known and someone is close by. As your expertise builds you take the harder ones, and your exposure to customers grows with it: from written answers, to calls, to being in the room when a customer wants their most pressing problem solved now.
This goes well beyond tickets. We are a fast-moving organisation and a lot of what needs to exist does not exist yet. You will take on and drive initiatives that make the whole operation scale: a recurring problem that should be solved once rather than fifty times, a piece of tooling that does not exist, a way of working that has outgrown itself. Interns here have shipped things that the team still uses.
How we think about ownership
You will be given real work with real consequences, early, because that is the only way anyone learns this job properly. The other half of that is judgement: explore and decide for yourself where you can, and pull someone in when something critical is on the line. Knowing which situation you are in is part of the skill, and nobody will hold it against you for asking. What matters is that you are the face of blp to that customer, and that you take that seriously.
Most of our customers work in German and you will be in front of them from early on. That is uncomfortable for about three weeks and then it is the best part of the job.
This is a real internship, not an observation post. You will be trusted with live customers quickly, with people close by while you learn.

title: Software Engineer, Search Infrastructure
description:
About the Team

The Search Product Infrastructure team builds the systems that power search experiences across ChatGPT. We partner with teams developing models, operating inference infrastructure, building specialized search experiences, and maintaining search indexes to bring advances in models and retrieval into production. Our work spans search orchestration, model serving, experimentation, and distributed systems, with direct impact on answer quality, responsiveness, reliability, and efficiency at ChatGPT scale.

About the Role

As a senior engineer on the Search Product Infrastructure team, you will design, build, and operate the systems that connect models with search at ChatGPT scale. You will tackle challenges in search orchestration, inference efficiency, experimentation, and production reliability, making tradeoffs that directly shape answer quality and user experience. Working closely with researchers and partner engineering teams, you will own projects from technical design through launch and iteration, evolving the architecture as models, product capabilities, and demand grow.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

- Design and evolve the services that coordinate search classification, retrieval, ranking, and model inference, working closely with researchers and partner engineering teams to bring new capabilities into production.

- Improve end-to-end latency, throughput, and infrastructure efficiency through profiling, caching, request routing, and capacity planning, making informed tradeoffs between search quality, reliability, and compute cost.

- Build experimentation tooling and automation to run reproducible A/B tests, define success metrics, and measure product impact. Use shadow traffic and load testing to validate system behavior, estimate capacity needs, and support safe production rollouts.

- Own production reliability through observability, resilient fallback behavior, incident response, and automation that improves launch safety and reduces operational toil.

- Build search APIs and tool interfaces that enable models and agents to retrieve information reliably while respecting access controls and preserving source attribution.

You might thrive in this role if you:

- Have significant experience designing, building, and operating large-scale distributed systems, with depth in performance, reliability, or resource efficiency.

- Bring experience in one or more of search, information retrieval, ML infrastructure, inference serving, or other high-throughput online systems.

- Have strong programming and systems debugging skills, and are comfortable working across languages and unfamiliar parts of a production stack.

- Can turn ambiguous product or research needs into clear technical plans, align partners across teams, and carry projects through deployment and measurable results.

- Enjoy learning across systems and ML, investigating unfamiliar problems, and sharing technical decisions and lessons clearly with others.

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. 

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

title: Technical Program Manager

description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About the Team

Core Technology is the engineering backbone of Anduril's hardware platforms - the shared systems, components, and infrastructure that power products across every division. The team develops and sustains the critical electromechanical systems, drive systems, propulsion, actuation, and embedded electronics that make Anduril's autonomous systems work. 

About the Role

We're looking for a Technical Program Manager to own the planning, execution, and delivery of hardware development programs within Core Tech. You'll be the connective tissue between design engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, test, and operations - driving complex electromechanical products from concept through production. You'll work directly with engineering leads to build roadmaps, track milestones, manage risks, and make sure the right teams are engaged at the right time. If you've driven hardware programs and want to do it at startup speed on systems that matter, this is the role.

What You’‘ll Do

• Represent and help build your program’s culture. As the liaison to the engineering development organization you are well positioned to consistently interact with all teams at Anduril and often will be tasked to represent the program in a cross-functional capacity. You should be knowledgeable of not only the current state of the program, but also the various technical and operational factors which define the product architecture and overall vision.

• Establishing key milestones and targets from across the organization to help define the product roadmap. This will require an in-depth understanding of what teams are affected by the various stages of your program’s engineering development. You are to ensure that teams are being engaged at the right time and at the right maturity stage to be successful. The roadmap you help develop would be the guide for your program that the organizations would reference and plan around.

• Evaluate and prioritize the various tasks required to successfully support the program development efforts. Be prepared to help drive to the best decision for the program and company. This generally should be a data driven approach, and should include inputs from all the various stakeholders to ensure the decision is well informed and can be successfully executed.

• Execute a variety of tasks to ensure the program stays on track. These tasks can take many forms as the engineering program manager should be prepared to fill any gap to de-risk the roadmap.

• Communicate engineering strategy and vision to the technical stakeholders to help manage expectations. Ensure all risks are noted and addressed with adequate time and resources to help keep things on track.

• Expected to work closely with teams including, but not limited to: design engineering, finance, logistics, EHS, manufacturing, supply chain, engineering testing, legal, technical operations, business strategy/programs, and production

Licensed Mental Health Counselor (LMHC) $70 K-85K/yr

Position Requirement: Remote Full-Time and Part-time Positions Available

If you are looking for a new opportunity to grow with a clinician founded and clinician led organization, look no further! As an authentic, unique, and skilled counselor, you have a plethora of options when it comes to work. Hospitals, community clinics, investment bank funded group practice startups, state agencies, and more.

At OptiMindHealth , we continuously strive to provide consistent, high-quality care and expand the reach of mental health care services in our communities. Unfortunately, the need often outpaces the services available to those we serve and only adds to the current mental health crisis in our nation. To combat this crisis and further our mission, we need more compassionate and skilled clinicians to join our cause. We are not interested in the “burnt-out” clinician that no longer finds meaning in their work and is just going through the motions; we are seeking people with a passion to provide excellent care, and the belief that we, together, can make a difference. If that’s you, then you’re in the right place!

Our approach with our team is simple, we take care of you, the clinician, so you can take care of patients. How do we do that? By investing in your growth, supporting you financially, holistically, and professionally, while being flexible regarding your personal needs and goals. The work we do with patients is hard enough and over the years we have found that our team often does their best work when the administrative burdens are taken off their plate and they are able to be fully present with their patients. Our administrative support team handles all non-clinical tasks so that you don’t have to think about anything except focusing on your patients.

Why bother with the endless administrative burdens and isolation of private practice? Use your highly trained interpersonal skills to change the culture around mental health care, decrease stigma, and help people who need you, while being supported by an experienced multi-disciplinary team of clinicians. Let us take care of the rest!

Want to work part time? No problem. Want to do group therapy? Sure! Want to do long-term psychodynamic psychotherapy with all of your clients? We do it every day. Interested in treating couples? We can make that happen. Basically, what we are saying is that whatever outpatient care you are interested in providing, we can surely accommodate you. We know you have exceptional skills; we want you to be part of our team.

The perfect candidate will share our passion for improving and expanding access to high quality mental health care and will thrive in a culture that emphasizes creativity, authenticity, humor, compassion, acceptance, and determination. Telehealth or onsite, we support your authentic and unique growth trajectory, while being yourself and having some fun!

We prioritize the clinician's experience by offering excellent compensation, benefits, training/supervision, and flexibility. • Starting Salary range: $70,000.00 - $85,000.00 per year.

• 401K with maximum employee matching.

• Health care benefits.

• Generous paid vacation and sick leave time.

• Paid administrative time for consultation, supervision, and documentation.

• Full administrative support.

Here are a few extra perks our team loves:

• Paid supervision, clinical rounds, and administrative time.

• Customized schedules within available clinic hours.

• Hybrid work environment if desired: Telehealth and/or in-person (in select locations).

• Muti-disciplinary team approach to treatment.

• Incredible administrative support team.

• Company leadership that understands the practice of mental healthcare.

title: Chief Risk Officer (CRO) – Retail Banking
description:
Position Summary
The Chief Risk Officer (CRO) - Retail Banking is responsible for establishing and leading the enterprise-wide risk management framework for the retail banking business. The CRO oversees credit, operational, market, liquidity, compliance, fraud, cyber, conduct, and reputational risks while ensuring alignment with the bank's strategic objectives, regulatory requirements, and risk appetite.
The role provides independent oversight and challenge to business activities, safeguarding the institution's financial stability, customers, and reputation while enabling sustainable growth.
Key Responsibilities
Enterprise Risk Management

• Develop and maintain the retail banking risk management framework.

• Establish risk appetite statements, risk limits, and governance standards.

• Ensure effective identification, assessment, monitoring, and mitigation of risks.

• Provide independent oversight of business decisions and strategic initiatives.

• Promote a strong risk culture throughout the organization.

Credit Risk Management

• Oversee retail credit portfolios, including:

• Mortgages

• Personal Loans

• Credit Cards

• Auto Loans

• Consumer Finance Products

• Establish underwriting standards and credit policies.

• Monitor portfolio quality, delinquency trends, and loss performance.

• Lead stress testing and credit risk scenario analyses.

• Recommend risk-adjusted lending strategies.

Operational Risk Management

• Develop frameworks to identify and manage operational risks.

• Monitor operational incidents, control failures, and emerging risks.

• Oversee business continuity and operational resilience programs.

• Strengthen internal controls and risk reporting mechanisms.

• Ensure effective risk and control self-assessment processes.

Regulatory Compliance & Conduct Risk

• Ensure compliance with banking regulations and consumer protection laws.

• Oversee conduct risk management and fair customer treatment initiatives.

• Maintain strong relationships with regulatory authorities.

• Lead regulatory examinations and risk-related audits.

• Ensure implementation of regulatory changes and risk controls.

Fraud & Financial Crime Risk

• Oversee fraud prevention, detection, and investigation programs.

• Strengthen anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-terrorist financing controls.

• Monitor financial crime risks and emerging threats.

• Ensure effective transaction monitoring and suspicious activity reporting.

• Collaborate with law enforcement and regulatory agencies when necessary.

Market & Liquidity Risk Oversight

• Monitor interest rate risk and liquidity risk exposures.

• Evaluate balance sheet vulnerabilities and stress scenarios.

• Support asset-liability management activities.

• Ensure adherence to regulatory capital and liquidity requirements.

Cybersecurity & Technology Risk

• Oversee technology and cyber risk governance.

• Assess cybersecurity threats and resilience capabilities.

• Ensure robust controls for digital banking platforms.

• Monitor third-party and vendor risk exposures.

• Support digital transformation initiatives through effective risk management.

Governance & Reporting

• Present risk reports to Executive Management, Risk Committees, and the Board.

• Develop key risk indicators (KRIs) and risk dashboards.

• Ensure timely escalation of significant risk issues.

• Maintain effective risk governance structures and committee frameworks.

Leadership & Talent Development

• Lead risk management teams across multiple disciplines.

• Develop future risk leaders and succession plans.

• Foster a culture of accountability, integrity, and transparency.

• Promote collaboration across business, compliance, audit, and technology functions.

Qualifications
Education

• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, Business Administration, Risk Management, Mathematics, or a related discipline.

• Master's degree (MBA, Finance, Economics, Risk Management, or related field) preferr

Trendyol’da Sizi Neler Bekliyor?
- FlexBenefits: Günlük yemek bütçeni özelleştirebilir, sağlık sigortanı upgrade edebilir, akaryakıt desteği veya Trendyol alışveriş bakiyesi gibi ek haklar arasından ihtiyacına göre seçim yapabilirsin.

title: Global Security Operations Center Manager
description:
Your Impact at LILA

The GSOC Manager will lead and operate Lila Sciences' Global Security Operations Center, owning the physical security technology stack and day-to-day security and intelligence operations for all sites globally. This role is responsible for enterprise access control management, Emergency Notification System (ENS) management, radio system management, visitor management, video surveillance, and intrusion detection systems, and acts as the central point of coordination for incident response and first-responder engagement. The GSOC Manager will build and maintain the SOPs, policies, and plans that govern GSOC operations, and will work in close, daily partnership with all Lila employees, the Senior Director - Protective Security, all facilities' security officers, Facilities, EHS, IT, contractors, building engineers, guests, and other third parties to keep Lila Sciences' people and sites safe and secure.

What You'll Be Building

• Manage day-to-day GSOC operations across all Lila Sciences sites, ensuring consistent 24/7 coverage and clear on-call/escalation procedures.

• Manage the enterprise access control system, including badge creation, access provisioning and deprovisioning, periodic access reviews, and compliance requirements.

• Manage enterprise visitor management processes, including visitor registration, screening, and temporary access issuance.

• Monitor and manage the enterprise video surveillance system, including active surveillance, camera health, footage review, and retention practices.

• Monitor and manage the intrusion detection system (IDS) and associated alarms.

• Serve as the primary interface with police, fire, EMS, and other first responders during security or safety incidents.

• Lead initial incident response coordination and triage for security-related events, escalating appropriately to leadership.

• Monitor 24/7 security operations and incident reporting across all sites.

• Write, maintain, and continuously improve GSOC SOPs, security policies, and emergency response plans.

• Monitor threat intelligence feeds and author threat intelligence reports and briefings for stakeholders.

• Track and monitor the locations and travel of executives and other traveling staff to support duty-of-care and travel-risk decisions.

• Partner closely with onsite security officers, Facilities, EHS, IT, contractors, building engineers, guests, and third parties to coordinate security activity across all sites.

• Maintain incident logs, GSOC metrics, and reporting for leadership review.

What You'll Need to Succeed

• Bachelor's degree in security management, criminal justice, emergency management, or a related field, or equivalent work experience.

Our job is to make the green travel choice the best choice. By building a better train travel experience, we help more people choose rail - creating a positive impact for customers, our business and the planet.

Introducing the Trainline Financial Control Team 👋

Trainline is Europe's leading independent rail platform, helping millions of travellers find and book the best value rail and coach journeys across our app, website and partner channels. Our Financial Control team sits at the heart of how we understand and run the business, owning the quality and integrity of our management accounts, balance sheet and month end processes. - Lead the team within Financial Control, principally through two direct reports, acting as a role model who coaches and mentors to build capability, delegates effectively, holds the team to a high standard of delivery and keeps development and succession front of mind

- Act as a thought leader within the team, bringing structure and clarity to complex or ambiguous problems and documenting conclusions so they can be applied consistently across the function

- Lead cross-functional projects from beginning to end, working with teams including Legal, Commercial, Product and Technology, setting and holding a timeline and navigating senior stakeholder relationships to land a single, well-documented position

- Hold accountability for the smooth, timely running of month end, including balance sheet integrity, key reconciliations and working capital analysis, with the team owning execution and you providing judgement and sign off, critically reviewing management accounts output for risks, inconsistencies and control gaps and ensuring a consistently high-quality, on-time, audit-ready close

- Act as the subject matter expert for external reporting and controls, providing technical challenge on Annual Report and Half-Year Report verification activity, owning accounting policy judgements and their documentation, and liaising with external auditors on balance sheet and reporting matters as needed

As the PM for Growth at Factory, you’ll own our overall approach to get users active and productive on the platform.

You’ll be responsible for our activation metric: how do we measure what it means to be an activated user, and how do we get more users to that point and beyond, whether they’re coming from our self-serve product or onboarding via an enterprise deployment.

And you’ll own our self-serve product offering: what we provide as part of it, how we price and package it, the role it plays in our broader company strategy, and how we should evaluate its success.

There won’t be a single “growth” engineering team to work with-you’ll operate across multiple engineering pods and work closely with our Marketing, BizOps, and Deployment functions to make sure we’re doing the right things to create more happy Factory users.

You’ll need a strong thesis for what makes a compelling early software factory experience in a competitive market, and an opinion about how PLG best reinforces a top-down Enterprise motion. You’ll need sharp technical instincts, genuine empathy for developers, and the ability to make fast, high-quality decisions in ambiguity. Our goal with the product function at Factory is to be high-leverage, high-ownership, and hands-on-you can expect to be working directly with the C-suite at the largest companies in the world, and shipping improvements directly to the product. And you’ll be central to defining the role of Product in a software factory-driven organization-a pattern we intend to pioneer and then help distribute across our customer base and the broader industry.

WHAT YOU WILL DO AND ACHIEVE

- Own the roadmap for multiple major areas of our product

- Partner closely with customers and work closely with data to understand pain points and translate them into product improvements.

- Work with engineering and research to ship features that keep Factory at the frontier of AI-powered development.

One Identity · Information Security, Attack Surface
Principal individual contributor · India · Reports to the Director of Information Security
Why this role exists
The architecture set in this role decides which certifications One Identity can hold and which markets we can sell into. That is unusual commercial weight for an engineering seat, and it comes with a mandate from leadership to build the program behind it.
We sell on-premises and hosted solutions. Some products run as hosted services we operate in Azure and AWS. Others ship as software customers deploy in their own datacenters. Infrastructure security here has two audiences: the environments we run, and the base images, container definitions, and deployment defaults we publish, which become part of every customer's environment. A hardening decision made once is inherited by everyone who deploys it.
We're separating from Quest Software and building an independent security function. The team is lean and globally distributed, and this role is its senior technical voice. Scope comes from what you design and automate, and from what engineering chooses to adopt.
What you'll do
Shape the architecture

• Own security architecture across Azure and AWS: tenant, subscription and account design, network segmentation and traffic control, private connectivity, egress policy, workload isolation. Where a regulated market or a certification constrains a design, you're expected to know before it's committed.

• Run our own products against real security requirements and tell us what you find. IT operates our privileged access controls on One Identity software, so you'll see how our products hold up under production pressure and take that back to the teams building them.

• Bring engineering into architectural decisions early. Designs teams help shape are the ones that hold up in production.

Raise the engineering bar

• Teams already build with infrastructure as code across both clouds. Raise the security ceiling inside that practice: hardened modules, secure-by-default landing zones and account baselines, and patterns teams reach for because they're better.

• Extend policy as code across the pipeline and the platform so teams get a signal at commit time.

• Own the hardened image pipeline for virtual machines and containers, covering the fleet we run and the images we publish: build, patch cadence, provenance, signing, and the automation that keeps both current.

• Secure the container orchestration layer, including the reference architecture and secure defaults customers inherit when they deploy our products on their own clusters.

• Set the security architecture for AI workloads: model and inference endpoint exposure, data boundaries and residency, identity for agents and service principals, secrets handling, and guardrails around AI tooling in the development lifecycle.

Reduce exposure and prove it

• Own infrastructure vulnerability and exposure management end to end: discovery, prioritization weighing exploitability and reachability alongside severity, ownership routing, remediation tracking, verification. • Elevate cloud posture and workload protection into a single practice spanning Azure and AWS. You set the platform direction, the coverage standard both clouds are held to, and the path findings take to the teams that own them.

Where a person still has to act, the finding arrives with owner, fix path, and rationale. Where we can act ourselves, it arrives as a pull request against the module, image definition, or policy that produced it. PRs, not tickets.

The Director, Financial Reporting & Internal Controls is responsible for the Company’s consolidated financial reporting, technical accounting, global statutory reporting and audit activities, and oversight of the internal control environment. This role will oversee a small team, providing day-to-day leadership, coaching, workload prioritization and performance support while ensuring high-quality execution of key reporting and control deliverables. The role partners closely with senior finance leadership, regional finance teams, cross-functional stakeholders and external auditors.

Key Responsibilities

• Prepare the Company’s quarterly and annual consolidated financial statements and related disclosures in accordance with IFRS.

• Ensure consistency and accuracy of financial reporting across the organization.

• Lead the consolidated financial statement audit, acting as the primary relationship manager with external auditors, coordinating key deliverables, reviewing and participating in the negotiation of audit fees, and resolving audit and accounting matters.

• Serve as a key technical accounting resource and lead the assessment and documentation of complex and non-routine transactions under IFRS, including revenue recognition, share-based compensation, leases, pensions, restructuring and provisions, impairments, business combinations, legal entity restructuring and other complex accounting matters.

• Monitor new accounting standards and developments and assess their impact on the Company’s financial reporting and accounting policies.

• Oversee global statutory financial statements, audits and required filings across multiple jurisdictions, including managing the statutory audit calendar, coordinating with local finance teams, external auditors and service providers, monitoring progress and driving timely completion.

• Oversee the financial internal control environment, including monitoring key controls, identifying control gaps and supporting remediation activities.

• Partner with Tax, Treasury, Legal and other functions on significant transactions, restructurings and other accounting matters.

• Support acquisitions, integrations, legal entity restructurings and other strategic initiatives from an accounting and financial reporting perspective.

• Drive continuous improvement and standardization of financial reporting, statutory audit and related finance processes.

• Lead, coach and develop a small team, including setting priorities, assigning work, providing timely feedback and supporting professional growth.

• Promote a collaborative, high-performance team environment with clear expectations, effective communication and accountability for deliverables.

• Support ad hoc projects and transactions as required.

Requirements

• Must hold a recognized professional accounting designation (CPA, ACA, or ACCA).

• 10+ years of progressive accounting and financial reporting experience, preferably including experience in a large multinational organization and/or public accounting.

• Strong knowledge of IFRS.

• Experience in preparing consolidated financial statements and related disclosures.

• Strong technical accounting research and documentation skill
